expectations.name: sample_counter_goes_stale
expectations.detail: event:guard_warn not observed within 13s after fault_fired (seq 0) [BLOCKED: context_valid is never set true by safety_core_build_input() (firmware/SaftyFW/src/tasks/safety_core.c) -- S13's staleness tracking (state->s13_stale_elapsed_s/s13_warn) lives inside safety_guards.c's context_valid-gated else-branch and is force-reset to 0/false while context_valid is false, so this cannot warn against present-day SaftyFW regardless of what the fixture does.]

blocked_on.reason: context_valid is never set true by safety_core_build_input() (firmware/SaftyFW/src/tasks/safety_core.c) -- S13's staleness tracking (state->s13_stale_elapsed_s/s13_warn) lives inside safety_guards.c's context_valid-gated else-branch and is force-reset to 0/false while context_valid is false, so this cannot warn against present-day SaftyFW regardless of what the fixture does.
blocked_on.phase: Phase 7 (link_task) is built and already publishes this context, sample_counter included -- link_task_publish_ context()/link_task_get_context_snapshot() (firmware/SaftyFW/ src/tasks/link_task.c) parse and cache every SAFETY_CMD_PUSH_CONTEXT (0x07) frame today, and context_zone_t.sample_counter (snapshots.h) is already part of that decoded struct. The real gap is one layer up: safety_core.c's safety_core_build_input() never calls link_task_get_context_snapshot() at all (see its own TODO at safety_core.c:208-210), so context_valid stays at its zero-init false regardless of what the ESP sends. A wiring gap in an already-built producer/consumer pair, not a missing Phase 7 deliverable.
